title: Aspect and tense on one timeline
summary: Most Polish verbs come in pairs. The imperfective verb looks at the action as a process or a habit; the perfective verb looks at one finished result. Together they give five forms.
note: A perfective verb has no present tense: przeczyta looks like a present form but means the future.

forms.name: Present
forms.summary: Happening now, or as a habit. Only imperfective verbs have a present tense.

scene.label: Now
scene.description: The reading is going on at the moment of speaking.

forms.name: Past
forms.summary: A process in the past: how long it went on, or what was happening. It does not say if it was finished.

scene.label: Process in the past
scene.description: The reading went on for some time yesterday; we do not know if Ola finished the book.

example.pl: Wczoraj Ola czytała książkę przez dwie godziny.
example.en: Yesterday Ola spent two hours reading a book.

forms.name: Past
forms.summary: One finished action with a result: the whole book is read.

scene.label: Result in the past
scene.description: At one point in the past the reading was finished; the result is there.

example.en: Ola has already read this book.

forms.name: Future
forms.summary: A process in the future: będzie + the infinitive (or + the past-tense form that agrees with the subject: będzie czytała / będzie czytał).

scene.label: Process in the future
scene.description: Tomorrow evening the reading will go on for some time.

example.pl: Jutro Ola będzie czytać cały wieczór.
example.en: Tomorrow Ola will be reading all evening.

forms.name: Future
forms.summary: One finished result in the future, formed like a present tense.

scene.label: Result in the future
scene.description: By Friday the reading will be finished.

example.pl: Ola przeczyta tę książkę do piątku.
example.en: Ola will have read this book by Friday.
